sources.citation: Starostin, George. 2017. Annotated Swadesh wordlists for the Fur-Amdang group (Fur family): Fur, Amdang. The Global Lexicostatistical Database (Moscow: RSUH / Santa Fe Institute), text version created 10/04/2017, 29 pp. [Amdang data from Wolf 2010 (Sounta primary; Kouchane, Yaouada, Tere in notes), Jungraithmayr 1971, Doornbos & Bender 1983; with 'Notes: General' and 'Transcription' sections on Amdang.]
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No statement on Amdang tone or stress. The transcription notes discuss only segmental conventions and say no phonological description of Amdang exists; Fur is described (after Jakobi 1990, Kutsch Lojenga & Waag 2004) as having two tonal registers H/L. Amdang forms are cited from Wolf without her sporadic IPA stress marks, while forms quoted from Doornbos & Bender 1983 keep tone diacritics (e.g. báŋ 'mountain/stone', p. 65 of that source) -- wordlist-level evidence only.

sources.citation: Wolf, Katharina. 2010. Une enquête sociolinguistique parmi les Amdang (Mimi) du Tchad: Rapport technique. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2010-028. 96 pp.
sources.note: Nothing stated. Sociolinguistic survey (vitality, dialect perception, literacy attitudes) with no phonology/tone/accent section; the only hit for 'accent' is about foreign accent in an FSI proficiency scale. Annexe D survey wordlists (Kouchane, Sounta, Yaouada, Téré, collected 2004) are phonetic IPA and carry IPA primary-stress marks on some items without comment (p. 41: kuˈri 'poule', duguˈdi 'queue', kɑˈmɑl 'chameau', ˈnɑmɑr 'éléphant'); the reproduced literature lists (Jungraithmayr 1971, Doornbos) use tone diacritics instead. sources.citation: Chan, Eugene S. L. (ed.). 2007. Numeral Systems of the World's Languages: Amdang. Data provided by Dr. Angelika Jakobi (University of Bayreuth), 13 May 2007, collected in N'Djamena c. 2000. Leipzig: MPI-EVA lingweb page.
sources.note: No prose statement. Jakobi's numerals are fully tone-marked with H/L on every syllable (wʊ̀k 1, ɲʊ́ŋ ~ íyɔ́ŋ 2, ít 3, ɔ̀ŋɔ́l 4, wát 5, ʊ́kkɛ́ːl 7, íʃʃɛ́ːl 8, bɔ̀rbɔ̀r 9, bɔ́k 10, bɔ́kkɛ̀rɛ́ wʊ̀k 11), i.e. the Fur specialist who wrote the 2002 sketch transcribes Amdang as a two-level tone language -- wordlist-only evidence, not a statement.
